commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to heave the weight up

description: The classic single-joint arm builder. Curling a dumbbell with strict form isolates the biceps and builds the mind-muscle connection every other arm exercise relies on.

commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare and drift
Bouncing the bar off the forehead
Using the shoulders to heave the weight
Going too heavy and losing the stretch
tips: Have a spotter or use dumbbells when going heavy
The slight backward arm angle keeps tension on the triceps
Control the descent — this exercise punishes ego

name: Dumbbell Concentration Curl
description: Maximum isolation: studies rank it among the highest biceps-activating exercises. Pure mind-muscle connection.
instructions: Sit on a bench with feet flat and knees apart.
Rest the back of your upper arm against your inner thigh.
Hold the dumbbell with arm extended toward the floor.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps hard and twist the pinky up at the top.
Lower slowly back to full extension.
Keep the upper arm pinned to your thigh throughout.
commonMistakes: Swinging the weight up
Lifting the elbow off the thigh
Going too heavy and shortening the range
Dropping the weight fast
tips: Light weight, perfect squeeze — this is a finisher
The supinating twist at the top maximizes the peak
Do these last in the arm workout when the biceps are pumped

name: Dumbbell Lunge
description: Unilateral leg strength that fixes imbalances and builds athletic single-leg power.
instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward into a long stride.
Lower until both knees are near 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and front knee over the ankle.
Drive through the front heel to step back.
Alternate legs each rep.
commonMistakes: Taking too short a stride and jamming the knee
Letting the front knee cave inward
Leaning the torso far forward
Pushing off the back foot instead of the front heel
tips: Longer strides hit glutes; shorter strides hit quads
Reverse lunges are kinder on the knees
Keep the dumbbells at your sides, not swinging

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: The hardest bodyweight leg exercise there is. Builds quads and glutes while torching your balance.
instructions: Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench, back to it.
Rest the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Keep your torso upright and core braced.
Lower until your front thigh is near parallel to the floor.
Keep the front knee tracking over the ankle.
Drive through the front foot to stand.
Complete all reps, then switch legs.
commonMistakes: Standing too close or too far from the bench
Letting the front knee cave inward
Pushing off the back foot
Rounding the torso forward
tips: Start with bodyweight — balance is the first challenge
A slight forward torso lean is fine; collapsing is not
Hold dumbbells once bodyweight feels easy

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: The number-one glute builder. Heavy hip extension without the spinal loading of deadlifts.
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench, bar over your hips.
Roll the bar into your hip crease with a pad for comfort.
Plant your feet flat, knees bent.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips.
Finish with hips fully extended and glutes squeezed.
Lower slowly back to the start.
Keep your chin tucked and ribs down.
commonMistakes: Overextending the lower back at the top
Letting the knees cave inward
Bouncing the bar off the hips
Craning the neck back
tips: Pause two seconds at the top of every rep
A thick bar pad makes heavy sets comfortable
Drive the knees out slightly to keep the glutes firing

name: Goblet Squat
description: The perfect squat teacher. The front-loaded weight keeps you upright and builds the pattern for barbell squats.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell vertically at chest height, cupping the top.
Set your feet just outside shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Brace your core and keep the weight close.
Sit down between your heels, elbows tracking inside the knees.
Descend until your hip crease is below your knees.
Drive through your whole foot to stand.
Keep your chest proud throughout.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward
Rounding the lower back at the bottom
Holding the weight away from the body
Rising onto the toes
tips: Elbows touching the inner knees is your depth check
The counterbalance lets most people squat deeper safely
Master this before touching a barbell

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
description: Single-leg strength with real-world carryover — stairs, hiking, sport. Kind on the back, brutal on the legs.
instructions: Stand facing a knee-height bench or box, dumbbells at your sides.
Place one foot flat on the bench.
Drive through the heel to stand up on the bench.
Bring the trailing foot up without pushing off it.
Step back down with control.
Complete all reps on one leg, then switch.
commonMistakes: Pushing off the trailing foot
Letting the knee cave inward
Using a box that's too high
Dropping down uncontrolled
tips: The working leg does everything — the other just balances
Start with bodyweight to find the right box height
Drive the opposite knee up at the top for extra glute work

name: Glute Bridge
description: Wakes up dormant glutes and builds the hip extension pattern. The foundation before hip thrusts.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Rest your arms at your sides.
Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips.
Finish with knees, hips, and shoulders in a straight line.
Hold the top for one second.
Lower slowly back down.
Don't overarch the lower back at the top.
commonMistakes: Overextending the lower back instead of squeezing glutes
Letting the knees cave inward
Rushing through reps without the squeeze
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
tips: If you feel it in your back, reset and squeeze the glutes first
A resistance band above the knees adds a great challenge
Single-leg bridges are the natural progression

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: A wide-stance deadlift that favors the legs and spares the back. Build total-body pulling power.
instructions: Stand with feet wide, toes pointed out, shins close to the bar.
Hinge down and grip the bar inside your knees.
Drop your hips, chest up, back flat.
Brace hard and push the floor away.
Stand tall with hips fully extended and glutes squeezed.
Lower the bar by hinging the hips back first.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back off the floor
Letting the knees cave inward
Jerking the bar off the floor
Hyperextending at lockout
tips: Think leg press the floor away, not pull the bar up
Sumo rewards patience off the floor — don't yank
Flat shoes or barefoot keep you connected to the floor

name: Seated Calf Raise Machine
description: Targets the soleus — the deep calf muscle standing raises miss. Complete lower-leg development.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform.
Lower the knee pads onto your thighs and release the safety.
Let your heels drop for a deep stretch.
Press through the balls of your feet to rise.
Squeeze the calves hard at the top.
Lower slowly back into the stretch.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled.
commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom
Doing fast half reps
Letting the knees lift off the pads
Skipping the stretch

Pause at both the top and bottom of every rep
Pair with standing calf raises for complete calves

name: Russian Twist
description: Rotational core strength for the obliques. Builds a resilient midsection for sport and life.
instructions: Sit with knees bent, feet hovering or on the floor.
Lean back slightly to engage the abs.
Hold a weight or clasp your hands at chest level.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing the weight beside your hip.
Pause briefly, feeling the obliques work.
Rotate to the other side with control.
Keep the movement in the torso, not the arms.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back
Moving too fast with momentum
Holding the breath
Rotating only the arms, not the torso
tips: Feet on the floor makes it easier; hovering makes it harder
Slow down — the obliques work hardest under control
Keep the chest up and the spine long

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: The gold standard for lower abs. Demands grip, shoulders, and serious core control.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Engage your shoulders and let your body settle still.
Brace your core and raise your legs.
Lift until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.

Stop the set if you start swinging.
commonMistakes: Swinging the body for momentum
Only doing tiny knee tucks while aiming for straight legs
Shrugging the shoulders up
Dropping the legs fast
tips: Bent-knee raises are the honest starting point
Kill the swing by pausing dead still between reps
Toes-to-bar is the advanced progression, not the starting point

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: A dynamic oblique builder that keeps constant tension on the core. One of the most effective ab exercises measured.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands lightly behind your ears.
Lift your shoulders off the floor and extend your legs.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating the opposite elbow to it.
Extend the leg back out as you switch sides.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Exhale on each rotation.
Don't pull your head forward.
commonMistakes: Yanking the neck with the hands
Going too fast and losing tension
Not rotating the torso, just moving the legs
Holding the breath
tips: Slow is better — two seconds per side
Think armpit to opposite knee, not elbow to knee
Keep the lower back pressed into the floor

name: Mountain Climbers
description: Core stability meets conditioning. A plank that moves — great as a finisher or warm-up.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Quickly switch legs, like running in place.
Keep your hips level — don't pike up.
Breathe steadily throughout.
Maintain a straight body line.
commonMistakes: Piking the hips up high
Letting the lower back sag
Bouncing the head and neck
Going so fast the core disengages
tips: Slow climbers build more core than frantic ones

Great as a 30-second finisher between strength sets

name: Dead Bug
description: Teaches your core to stabilize while the limbs move — the foundation of a bulletproof back.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms reaching to the ceiling.
Lift your legs to tabletop, knees over hips.
Press your lower back flat into the floor.
Slowly extend one arm overhead and the opposite leg out.
Go only as far as your back stays flat.
Return with control and switch sides.
Exhale as you extend.

Moving too fast
Holding the breath
Extending further than control allows

name: Side Plank
description: Builds the obliques and lateral stability that front planks miss. Essential for a balanced core.
instructions: Lie on your side with your forearm on the floor, elbow under shoulder.
Stack your feet or stagger them for balance.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Keep your neck neutral.
Hold for the target time, then lower.
Repeat on the other side.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag
Rolling forward or backward
Shrugging the shoulder to the ear
Holding the breath
tips: Drop the bottom knee for an easier version
Think about pushing the floor away with your forearm
Quality over duration — reset when form breaks
